pending_articles.title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
pending_articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02486-8

The dimensionality of intrinsic brain connectivity systematically shapes how task representations compress and expand across the cortex, and activity flow modeling shows the active role of network geometry in generating the transformation.

pending_articles.title: Different modes of stimulation at the Neiguan acupoint (PC6) regulate different EEG microstates under VR immersion conditions
pending_articles.content: IntroductionAcupuncture at the Neiguan acupoint (PC6) alleviates postoperative and chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. Nevertheless, the central regulatory effects of PC6 stimulation on virtual reality motion sickness (VRMS), a form of physiological vertigo triggered by visual-vestibular sensory conflict, and the corresponding alterations in electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate characteristics remain unclear. Using EEG microstate analysis as the primary approach, this study investigated the effects of different PC6 stimulation modalities on dynamic brain functional changes during VRMS, aiming to further elucidate the potential neural mechanisms underlying acupoint stimulation in VRMS.MethodsParticipants were recruited based on their Motion Sickness Susceptibility Questionnaire scores, with a cut-off value of ≥34 used as the inclusion criterion. A total of 200 healthy participants were enrolled and randomly assigned to four equal groups (n = 50 per group): control (32 °C), 40 °C, 44 °C, and 2-Hz transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS). The experimental protocol consisted of three phases: baseline, active stimulation, and post-stimulation. All participants received a 40-min stimulation targeting the right PC6 acupoint. EEG data were continuously recorded throughout the experiment.ResultsMicrostate analysis revealed that during the stimulation phase, the 2-Hz TEAS group exhibited significantly increased duration, occurrence, and coverage of microstate D compared with the control group, whereas the 40 °C group affected only the duration of microstate D. During the post-stimulation phase, compared with the control group, the 44 °C group showed a decreased duration of microstate A and significantly increased duration and coverage of microstate B, while the 2-Hz TEAS group continued to exhibit sustained effects on the duration of microstate D.ConclusionThe neuroelectrophysiological signatures of stimulation at PC6 in modulating VRMS are predominantly reflected in the dynamic changes of microstates A, B, and D. Thermal stimulation and low-frequency electrical stimulation engage distinct central modulatory pathways, providing a neuroelectrophysiological basis for optimizing stimulation parameters for in future studies on VRMS.

pending_articles.title: Retraction: Intervention effect of rehabilitation robotic bed under machine learning combined with intensive motor training on stroke patients with hemiplegia
Overcoming subject variability in P300 decoding based on quantification by deep learning
pending_articles.content: Binary P300 decoding is a cornerstone of P300-based brain-computer interfaces, enabling applications such as assistive communication, neurorehabilitation, and cognitive monitoring. However, substantial subject variability in EEG patterns poses a major challenge to the development of generalized P300 decoders. To address this problem, this study proposes SQ_EMoE, a subject-variability-aware enhanced Mixture-of-Experts framework that uses the confidence produced by a deep subject-identification network as a practical proxy for trial-level subject distinctiveness. High-confidence trials are routed to subject-specific experts, whereas uncertain trials are redirected to a pooled general expert, allowing the framework to dynamically balance subject-specific specialization and cross-subject generalization. Latent subject representations are further visualized to qualitatively examine subject separability and its relationship with routing behavior. Experiments on eight random subjects from each of two public P300 datasets yielded mean ROC–AUC values of approximately 0.86 on BNCI Horizon 2020 and 0.89 on P300-LINI, outperforming pooled EEGNet and architecture-matched pooled P300MCNN baselines. Ablation experiments further demonstrated the contribution of confidence-controlled fallback to the general expert. To evaluate scalability, the framework was additionally tested on all 22 subjects of P300-LINI. With the original subject-identification network, SQ_EMoE achieved a mean ROC–AUC of 0.8518; after strengthening the subject representation and identification network, performance increased to 0.8760, exceeding the pooled P300MCNN baseline (0.8482) and slightly surpassing the oracle routing or within-subject decoding (0.8744). Leave-one-subject-out experiments further showed that the under-realized SQ_EMoE conservatively redirects most completely unseen-subject trials to the general expert when reliable subject-specific routing is unavailable. These results demonstrate that effective modeling of subject variability, together with adaptive integration of shared and subject-specific representations, provides a promising alternative to conventional one-size-fits-all EEG decoding.

pending_articles.title: Microglia in the neurogenic niche: emerging roles of immunometabolism
pending_articles.content: Adult neurogenesis is dynamically regulated by the neurogenic niche, yet the mechanisms governing its remodeling are not fully elucidated. Current research has increasingly extended beyond the intrinsic properties of neural stem cells to consider the broader microenvironment in which neurogenesis occurs, with microglia emerging as important regulators of the neurogenic niche. Drawing upon pathological contexts such as depression and aging, this review characterizes the hallmarks of neurogenic niche dysregulation and synthesizes the mechanisms by which microglia modulate neurogenic efficiency. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of immunometabolism in shaping microglial functional states and subsequent niche remodeling. We propose that microglial immunometabolic states may serve as an important interface through which pathological perturbations within the brain are linked to remodeling of the neurogenic niche, providing a conceptual framework for understanding neurogenic decline across distinct pathological contexts.
pending_articles.author: Yan Liu

pending_articles.title: Striatal and orbitofrontal grey matter volumes are associated with cognitive event related potentials during associative learning task performance in male and female children and adolescents
pending_articles.content: IntroductionThe individual differences in gray matter volumes and event-related potentials may underlie variability in associative learning. However, little is known about the sex differences in these structure–function relationships across development.MethodsThe current study investigates associations between local gray matter volumes and brain responses during associative learning task in children and adolescents aged 7–21 years. We hypothesized that gray matter volumes of the basal ganglia and prefrontal cortex would be associated with event-related potentials indices of associative learning, in a sex-dependent manner. Final analysis included 138 participants (68 females, 70 males). Participants completed an associative learning task with concurrent EEG event-related potentials recording. Gray matter volumes were analyzed within 5 a priori regions of interest, predominantly located in the basal ganglia vicinity and prefrontal cortex.ResultsIn females, anterior N400 latency to Early-stage stimulus onsets was positively associated with gray matter volume in the left putamen/lentiform nucleus and to Late-stage stimulus onsets with gray matter volume in the subgenual anterior cingulate. Anterior P300 amplitude to Late-stage feedback presentation was positively associated with gray matter volume in the right nucleus accumbens/putamen and the right medial orbitofrontal cortex. Correlations involving the subgenual anterior cingulate and medial orbitofrontal cortex were significantly stronger in the female group relative to the male group. In males, anterior P300 amplitude to Early-stage feedback presentation was associated with gray matter volume in a left hippocampus/amygdala cluster, yet not significantly differently from females. In exploratory analysis, after accounting for total brain volumes, age was positively associated with the volumes of striatal and orbitofrontal regions in both sexes, with largely overlapping patterns.DiscussionTherefore, findings support structure–function relationships linking gray matter volumes of striatum and orbitofrontal cortex to brain activity during reinforcement learning performance. Given that associative learning is an instance of reinforcement learning, its underlying neural processes are influenced by the structural development of striatal and orbitofrontal regions.
pending_articles.author: Almira Kustubayeva

pending_articles.title: The mammalian regulatory architecture: biobehavioral portals and the organization of physiological state
pending_articles.content: IntroductionNeuromodulatory interventions can produce overlapping adaptive outcomes despite engaging substantially different biological pathways. Pathway-centered approaches identify how interventions initially engage the nervous system and characterize pathway-specific mechanisms. Convergence across interventions raises an additional question: how can different biological routes influence overlapping domains of adaptive function?MethodsThis conceptual paper develops the Mammalian Regulatory Architecture (MRA), an organizational framework informed by identified mammalian synapomorphies (shared derived characteristics) and comparative anatomical, developmental, physiological, and functional observations.ResultsThe MRA hypothesizes that mammalian evolution reorganized relationships among conserved regulatory processes through their integration with mammalian specializations and regulatory demands associated with nursing, prolonged developmental dependency, caregiving, co-regulation, and reciprocal social communication. The framework provides the basis for a biological portal model of neuromodulation that distinguishes the pathway of initial engagement from the functional significance of that engagement within the broader regulatory architecture. Whereas the pathway identifies how an intervention initially engages the nervous system, its portal significance concerns how that engagement influences state-regulating processes within the MRA.DiscussionThe proposed framework reframes neuromodulation from a process defined primarily by its neural target or pathway to one in which pathway engagement may influence broader regulatory organization, physiological state, Accessibility—the state-dependent availability of existing adaptive capacities—and adaptive function. It offers an organizational account of how distinct biological routes may influence overlapping domains of adaptive function.

pending_articles.title: Continuous performance tests in the assessment of children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a narrative review
pending_articles.content: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is diagnosed primarily through clinical interviews, behavioral observations, and rating scales, while continuous performance tests (CPTs) provide complementary, performance-based measures of sustained attention, response inhibition, and response consistency. This narrative review compares major CPT paradigms used in pediatric ADHD assessment according to their cognitive targets, task characteristics, psychometric properties, ecological validity, clinical applications, and evidence maturity. Traditional standardized paradigms generally provide more established normative and psychometric frameworks, with the strongest support available for the Conners CPT series and TOVA, whereas distraction-enhanced, motion-integrated, virtual reality-based, and eye-tracking-integrated approaches extend assessment toward more complex and ecologically relevant behavioral contexts. Evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses supports group-level differences in core CPT measures, particularly reaction time variability, omission errors, and commission errors; however, substantial overlap across ADHD, psychiatric comorbidities, developmental stages, and other clinical conditions limits their specificity for individual diagnosis. Technology-enhanced paradigms may provide additional information regarding distractibility, motor activity, and gaze behavior, but their incremental clinical value remains uncertain because of heterogeneous methodologies, limited independent replication, and insufficient large-scale cross-cultural normative data. CPTs should therefore be interpreted as objective adjuncts within a multimodal assessment framework rather than as standalone diagnostic or subtype-classification tools. Future research should prioritize standardized outcome definitions, age-appropriate normative datasets, management of practice effects in repeated testing, and prospective multicenter studies evaluating whether specific CPT paradigms add clinically meaningful information beyond established diagnostic and treatment-monitoring procedures.
pending_articles.author: Xiaoke Zhao

pending_articles.title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and machine learning for outcome prediction in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective study of 353 patients
pending_articles.content: BackgroundAcute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Early prediction for clinical outcomes is essential for guiding therapy. Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) offers detailed characterization of ischemic tissue and may predict prognosis in AIS patients. This study assesses the prognostic value of multiparametric MRI parameters in predicting functional outcome, recurrence risk and mortality in AIS patients.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective analysis of 353 AIS patients who underwent multiparametric MRI within 24 h of onset. MRI metrics including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion volume, ADC minimum, perfusion parameters and Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging (SWI) microbleeds were correlated with National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores at discharge and 90 days. Predictive performance for clinical outcomes was assessed by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.ResultsAmong 353 AIS patients with a mean door-to-imaging time of 27 ± 10 min, higher NIHSS, larger DWI volume, prolonged mean transit time (MTT) and Tmax, and increased microbleeds significantly correlated with mortality and disability, while lower ADC, CBF, and CBV correlated inversely with clinical outcomes. NIHSS ≥10.5 and DWI lesion volume ≥52.5 mL yielded AUCs of 0.963 and 0.975 and accuracies of 91.35% and 92.79%, respectively; CBF ≤ 20.5 yielded an AUC of 0.975. NIHSS ≥8.5 and MTT ≥8.5 s showed AUCs of 0.948 and 0.931, respectively, for predicting hemorrhagic transformation. Perfusion thresholds modestly predicted 90-day recurrence (AUC = 0.7). Hypertension, diabetes, and prior stroke were significant clinical predictors of poor outcome. These predictive metrics reflect internal, within-cohort validation only; independent external validation is required before clinical application.ConclusionMultiparametric MRI provides robust prognostic information in AIS. Quantitative thresholds for perfusion and diffusion parameters help in risk stratification for hemorrhage and mortality, enhancing individualized management and outcome prediction.

recently_processed.title: Longitudinal Imaging in a Mouse Model of Focal Cortical Dysplasia Reveals Lesion Expansion and Loss of Pre-Discharge Neuronal Recruitment
recently_processed.content: ABSTRACT Objective: Focal cortical dysplasia type II (FCD II) is a leading cause of drug-resistant focal epilepsy, yet how its lesional circuits behave and change over time in vivo has not been directly observed. Methods: We used a mouse model of FCD II carrying the patient-derived gain-of-function mTORp.L2427P variant introduced by in utero electroporation. Through a chronic cranial window over the lesion, we performed repeated in vivo two-photon calcium imaging of identified dysmorphic neurons, pyramidal cells, and VIP interneurons at defined time points, combined with video-EEG monitoring, to determine seizure status and relate cellular activity to interictal discharges. Results: The lesion was not static in adulthood. Dysplastic cortex expanded progressively. This expansion occurred without the tenascin R/C accumulation reported in human FCD II, and was partly explained by continued somatic growth of dysmorphic neurons. Dysmorphic neurons were generally hypoactive; in seizing mice, both dysmorphic and pyramidal cell activity progressively declined, whereas VIP interneuron activity increased slightly in non-seizing animals. In non-seizing lesional cortex, neurons were reliably recruited immediately before interictal discharges. By late disease stages, pre-discharge recruitment had weakened to the point that lesional layer 2/3 neurons were no more active before discharges than expected by chance. Significance: These findings recast FCD II as a lesion that continues to remodel structurally and functionally throughout adulthood, and does so most markedly in animals with seizures. Growth, a cell-type-specific shift in spontaneous activity, and a progressive loss of the lesion's temporal lead over interictal discharges together suggest that FCD II is a dynamically evolving lesion whose relationship to epileptiform activity changes over time. If the lesion progressively loses its generative role, the window in which removing it can arrest the disease is finite, consistent with clinical evidence favoring earlier surgery.

recently_processed.title: Sex-dependent Aβ RA-Low threshold mechanoreceptors alteration in diabetic conditions
recently_processed.content: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a major complication of diabetes that profoundly affects quality of life, yet its cellular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Neuropathic pain and sensory loss in DPN are thought to arise from progressive alterations in peripheral nerves usually described as a glove-stocking distribution, but the specific contribution of sensory neuron subtypes has received little attention. Here, we focused on A{beta} rapidly adapting low-threshold mechanoreceptors (A{beta} RA-LTMRs), a large-diameter sensory neuron subtype best known for mediating touch and vibratory sensation. Using an intersectional genetic approach, we generated AdvillinCre; MafAFlpO; Ai65 mice, allowing us to selectively label MafA-expressing sensory neuronal populations, which we identified as A{beta} RA-LTMRs. We provide the first detailed characterization of how diet-induced type 2 diabetes alters A{beta} RA-LTMRs. After 16 weeks of high-fat diet (HFD), we observed striking sex-dependent effects. Male mice developed impaired glucose tolerance, mechanical hypoalgesia, and thermal hyperalgesia, which correlated with a decrease of A{beta} RA-LTMR central projections in the dorsal horn. By contrast, female mice showed no changes in either their glycemic status or their sensory sensitivity. These findings demonstrate that A{beta} RA-LTMRs are vulnerable to early diabetes-induced alterations in a sex-dependent manner and highlight distinct peripheral versus central mechanisms contributing to sensory dysfunction.

recently_processed.title: Technical Parameters and Feedback Control for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Enhancement by Focused Ultrasound
recently_processed.content: Focused ultrasound combined with intravenously infused microbubbles has been shown to effectively enhance the permeability of the blood-brain barrier, facilitating drug delivery to the brain. A wide range of technical parameters has been evaluated through preclinical studies and clinical trials. Generally, a low frequency between 200 and 300 kHz is preferred for the transcranial approach, while 1 MHz is used in implantable devices. Standard parameters include a burst length of 5 to 10 ms, a pulse repetition frequency of 0.2 to 10 Hz, and sonication durations of 90 to 180 seconds. A pressure magnitude around 0.46 mechanical index appears to be near the threshold for BBB permeability enhancement at standard microbubble dosage without causing hemorrhage. Various microbubble and nanobubble types have been tested at different doses, which in principle can be normalized by gas volume. Control methods that use harmonic emmisions for power feedback have been proposed to enhance consistency and account for patient variability, and these methods are currently being tested in several clinical trials.

recently_processed.title: Decoding Spikes From Multiunit Data
recently_processed.content: Communication and control in biological systems is mediated by the timing of discharges –spikes– from excitable cells such as neurons and muscle fibers. Each spike is associated to a characteristic waveform that can be captured by sensors. The waveform's characteristics depend on the cell's biophysical properties and the recording modality. Depending on the technique, e.g., electrical recordings with electrodes, optical imaging, ultrasound, the observed signals are mixtures of waveforms emitted from active cells/sources (multiunit data/signals). Recovering the timing and identity of these sources (multiunit or spike decoding) is central to neuroscience, clinical diagnostics, and neural interfacing, yet it remains challenging due to waveform superposition, non-stationarity, limited training labels, and the computational demands of high-density recordings. This review provides a unified methodological perspective on spike decoding by formalizing the problem as a sparse source separation task under a convolutive mixing model. Rather than organizing the literature by application domain, we group and critically compare methods by their underlying principles: classical spike sorting, Bayesian and probabilistic inference, blind source separation, and data-driven approaches, including deep learning and hybrid schemes. For each class of methods, we present the core mathematical formulation and algorithmic strategies and discuss assumptions and limitations. Our synthesis highlights parallels in signal processing across physical recording modalities and clarifies when and why particular approaches succeed or fail. By bridging previously compartmentalized literature, this survey aims to accelerate crosspollination of ideas between application areas and to provide a roadmap for selecting, adapting, and advancing decoding methods across diverse multiunit recording modalities.
